key_insight: Boron doping widens the stable mixed-valence window in Cu-O thin films, delaying the Cu2O→Cu4O3→CuO transition and enabling very low resistivity.
engineering_relevance: This offers a controllable route to tune copper-oxide absorber/contact properties for optoelectronic and photovoltaic devices via reactive sputtering and oxygen partial pressure.
method: Reactive magnetron sputtering of Cu-O thin films with controlled boron incorporation
Systematic variation of oxygen partial pressure to map phase evolution
Electrical and chemical characterization of phase, bonding, and resistivity
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a phase progression with increasing oxygen partial pressure and a best resistivity of about 0.06 Ω·cm in highly B-doped films, among the lowest reported for a CuO-like material.
watch_item: The improved conductivity is strongly tied to precise B content and oxygen partial pressure, so reproducibility and process control may be challenging when scaling deposition.
paper_title: Boron-assisted stabilization of low-resistivity mixed-valence Cu-O thin films prepared by reactive magnetron sputtering
